evidence.detail: Rows ac1/absent (no file, no folder; the paths are fixed in the probe), ac1/not-regular (a link, a folder), ac1/owner, ac1/mode (another group, 0755, 4750), ac1/folder (the holding folder owned by this user, a folder others may write, a link on the way), ac1/capability (none, not effective, inheritable, version 1, another capability), ac1/capability-exact (cap_dac_read_search added, a capability of the upper word), ac1/capability-root-id (version 3 with root id 100000 refused, with root id 0 used), ac1/no-pin, ac1/digest, ac1/no-socket, ac1/writer (the writer check left real: the stand-in's own status; another uid, a second capability, NoNewPrivs 0, no filter), ac1/writer-gone (the writer ends after its table and the status read is answered as a locked reader's: the pidfd refuses it), ac1/bytes-before-the-byte (a wrapper writes a table, then executes the built reader on a socket pair: the kernel's own status shows the process locked, and its table is refused; a table in the header's write; a table sent before the byte), ac1/second-writer, ac1/header-cap (cap=0 from the stand-in and from the built reader served on the socket, whose own status showed NoNewPrivs 1 and Seccomp 2), ac1/reader-locks-first (the built reader shows NoNewPrivs 1 and Seccomp 2 when its header arrives, sends nothing more until the byte, and the table after it), ac1/used. In every refused row the undumpable process in the item is judged by the bound as before and the in_use facts name the state and what was seen. Green: proof/VELDO-0344/suite-green.txt.

The rows run the real probe against real processes of the kernel's process table (python children; the unreadable ones call prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0); threads with a file system state or a descriptor table of their own by unshare), over a real unix socket served one program per connection as the socket unit serves it, with the kernel's SO_PASSCRED and SO_PASSPIDFD records and real pidfd looks, and with the reader built from its source by /usr/bin/cc and run for real. What a suite cannot have without root (the file's owner, group and mode, the folders' owners, the capability attribute, the capability lines of the writer's status) is given through the probe's seam and named as such in each row.

Eight cases, each red on its own row: space344-digest-not-compared (ac1/digest: a program that prints a table showing the process elsewhere is used and the process is not counted), space344-any-set-with-ptrace (ac1/capability-exact), space344-version-3-any-root-id (ac1/capability-root-id), space344-file-and-not-its-folders (ac1/folder), space344-header-cap-ignored (ac1/header-cap), space344-output-whoever-wrote-it (ac1/writer), space344-process-id-without-the-pidfd (ac1/writer-gone), space344-bytes-from-before-the-lock (ac1/bytes-before-the-byte: the wrapper's table is taken).

assumptions: NOT DONE: .veldo/policy.yaml. The spec's footprint and protected_paths name it, to protect the reader's source and the two unit templates. It is itself a protected path and the builder was told to touch none and to report. Nine entries are written out in proof/VELDO-0344/owner-install.txt: the six of the spec's protected_paths, and three the review names (finding 3): .veldo/control_space_probe.py, engine/.veldo/control_space_probe.py and docs/veldo-procread-setup.txt. Until the owner adds them none of those files is a protected path.

NOT RUN: everything that needs the installed reader. The builder has no sudo. Row ac6/installed (the reader check in a transient user unit with NoNewPrivileges=yes, reading an undumpable process and its second thread through the installed reader, with the run time recorded) printed its skip line, and its declared falsifier was not applied. The state used was reached only with a stand-in reader and with the capability facts given through the seam. So three things stay assumptions until the owner's host runs that row: cap_sys_ptrace held by the owner's uid reads root-owned entries (proved by the check's fifth line alone, the whole block of process 1; the other four lines read a process of the owner's own uid, which the kernel permits on another branch, as the review found); it reads the task entries; the two unit files work as written (Accept=yes, the capability arriving in the unit). Also unmeasured: how long the reader runs with the capability on the full table. Without it, it printed 3.6 MB for 373 processes in well under a second.

requires.json cannot name a row: it is derived by scripts/run_scope.py and holds suite closures only. It was regenerated for the new suite. The installed-only row is declared by its SELFTEST SKIP line and in the suite's requires_note in scripts/suites/manifest.json, which is how the namespace helper's rows are in fact declared.

AC7, THE PREFIX MAP DOES NOT CHANGE THE DIGEST. Measured on this compiler: with the map, without it, and compiled by an absolute path from another folder, the build has one digest, because the line carries no debug information and no folder name reaches the binary. The falsifier as worded (two folders give two digests) does not turn red. The row requires the map in the line and the registered case is red on that requirement alone. The spec's History records it.

WORDING OF TWO FALSIFIERS. "A program that prints an empty table ... the item reads free" (AC1) and "the row cuts the output ... the item reads free" (AC5): a process with no block stays unread and is counted by the bound, so no empty or cut table can make an item read free. The rows use the table that would: a whole block that shows the process elsewhere. For the cut, the row reads the process whose block came before the cut. On the host's own table the rows read one process's part of the answer (other processes of the host are judged too); the AC3 rows read the whole answer on a fixture table.

process_reader MAY BE LEFT OUT of the space section and then reads as none. Design 6.8 says every key is required. Nine reviewed suites outside this footprint write sections without it and suite 130 holds the required keys to the nine it names, so requiring it would turn them red. Left out, no reader is used.

EVERY THREAD, AND kcmp. Reading every task's descriptors took the probe from 0.1 to 1.7 seconds per call on this host. The probe asks the kernel with kcmp whether a task shares its descriptor table or its file system state with the first thread and reads it separately unless the kernel answers that they are the same one; any error has it read. The call number is known for x86_64 and aarch64; elsewhere every task is read. Inside a sandbox whose filter refuses kcmp the probe reads every task, which is slower and not less.

NO ROW for a call of another architecture, for the reader's exit 4 on a /proc that is not a process file system, or for the reader's 60 second unit limit. The first two are in the source (the filter's architecture and x32 tests; fstatfs before the header) and were read, not run: making either happen needs a 32-bit call path or a mount.

THE THREE OWNER COMMANDS ARE IN THE PROBE FILE, as the design's install lines name them. reader-units writes the two unit files through install(1), and the reader check makes three empty temporary folders. VELDO-0299's row probe/facts-only, which holds that the module calls nothing that writes, is green; a reviewer should know that this command exists beside the probes and that no probe function calls it.

The reader allows no call for memory (it keeps everything in static storage: about 60 MB of untouched address space), which is narrower than the list in design 7.1. A process with more than 524,288 distinct facts, or 65,536 tasks or mounts, gets an x line and stays unread.

A zombie of the owner's still counts by the bound with the reader used: its mountinfo cannot be read, the reader prints x mnt 22, and the block is unread. That is the behaviour before this ticket, not a new one.

On the owner's host, once the reader is installed and pinned, every in_use call of every suite that reads the host's own process table will go through the real reader. Suites 136 to 140 were only run here with the reader absent.

REVIEW FIX (review-veldo-0344.md, verdict FIX). The reader's source is unchanged (SHA-256 233df2c7174357a0d1481b279f60e679f52135bfaf1e5c7edc940866fdfb865c), so C, H and proof/VELDO-0344/reader.sha256 stand. The new sudo line was never run as root: its order and its removals are read by the row and were run by hand in a scratch folder with stand-ins. Beyond the review's form, the copy from standard input is part of the condition of the comparison and a failed step after the comparison also removes the copy, so that no failure leaves a file; the review asked for nothing left behind after a failed comparison. The fifth row assumes process 1 is root's and closed to the probe, which holds on the owner's host; where it does not, the row fails and the check does not pass. The design document's copy of the old sudo line (docs/design/VELDO-0295-design.md, section 7.1) is outside this spec's footprint and was NOT edited: it differs from the setup text until the lead amends it.

TOOLCHAIN RECORD, 2026-11-14. An unattended update of the C library on the build host (glibc 2.39-0ubuntu8.9 to 2.39-0ubuntu8.12) changed the digest of the reader's static build from bb9bd262a12793669e19a1cf3c77f2539ad48cb26093ba4377d5cf520d70d035 to 861d22a18e477344b637dae2d3443cb78a9233b3b0ee90620679f599fa47f199. The reviewed source is unchanged, byte for byte, and no code, suite or setup text changed. reader.sha256 keeps both records, each with its toolchain; owner-install.txt carries the new H and says H follows the toolchain and is read from the record reviewed for the installing host's toolchain. The new record is not reviewed yet: until it is, nothing is to be installed with it. The reader is not installed on this host, and no sudo command was run. Row ac7/recorded-digest compares the build with the record again on this host (it skipped while the record named the earlier library).

THE RUN LABEL (2026-11-14) IS READ ONLY WITHOUT THE CAPABILITY HERE. Rows reader/label and label/table run the built reader on processes this account may read, and the probe on tables the row composes. That the reader reads the label of a process the probe is refused (another uid, not dumpable) needs the installed capability: it is the sixth line of the reader check, which row ac6/installed requires and which has run nowhere. An undumpable process read without the capability gives x env 13 and a label that is not read, which the row asserts.

AC4'S TEXT IS NARROWER THAN THE READER NOW. It says the reader reads only stat, mountinfo, maps, cwd and fdinfo and prints numbers only. By the lead's decision it also reads the environ entry of each task and prints the value of one variable in hexadecimal. The builder did not edit the criterion; the rows ac4/format and ac4/entries assert what the reader does now. The source and its digest (reader.sha256, the first record) await review, and owner-install.txt says the source it names is not the reviewed one.

A LABEL IS WHAT A PROCESS'S ENVIRONMENT SAYS. The environ entry shows the environment a process was started with, which the process can overwrite, and a process between fork and exec shows its parent's. The CLI's own read of a readable process has the same limits. A value longer than 64 bytes is not printed and leaves the label unread, so such a process holds every run until it ends.

FIX AFTER THE REVIEW OF THE RUN LABEL (2026-11-15; review-veldo-0344-label.md, verdict FIX). Finding 1: an environment is taken as read only from a whole read of one program; what is not whole is x env 11, and the probe reads that as a label that was not read. The source changed, so its digest did: SHA-256 44936632a48945a9380319b91b32deef1e9ffac11bac477401db1691b14b3561, built bf1e1256ad3edb8fb83c695ef7e01380146a7048a3c465bfe463d9fee8835f26 with line 1 of owner-install.txt, twice, on cc 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1 and glibc 2.39-0ubuntu8.12. Both await review; owner-install.txt says the source of 2026-11-14 is not to be installed. No sudo command was run and nothing is installed.

WHAT NO ROW FALSIFIES IN THE WHOLE READ. The comparison of the two takings alone (start time, exe, the two ends of the environment): a complete read of the right length of a program the task no longer is cannot be made on purpose from outside the kernel, so no mutant of that comparison alone turns a row red. The second read: without it the reader is still right and says unread more often. The 150 reads of the process that executes itself are a race the row does not control: on this host the unfixed reader was wrong in 12 to 33 of 150 reads in every run made (the review's, the builder's by hand, and the mutant's), and a host where it is never wrong in 150 would leave space344-environment-not-whole-taken-as-read red only on the two processes that need no race.

AN ENVIRONMENT OF NO BYTES IS UNREAD, ALWAYS. A process that really has no environment therefore holds every run it could belong to for as long as it lives. The reason is in the mutant's own record: with only that condition gone, the reader said l - for the process that executes itself in 4 of 150 reads, because during an execution both ends of the environment can read zero before and after.

THE READER OPENS TWO MORE ENTRIES OF A TASK, its stat and its exe by stat, both beneath /proc and for reading, and prints nothing of either. AC4's text names neither; it was already narrower than the reader and was not edited. With the capability, the exe of a root-owned process is read by stat as its working directory is.

SEEN AND NOT CHANGED: a process whose first thread has ended and whose other thread then executes a program takes the first thread's id.
